title: Nan 3-Day Itinerary 2026 — Old Town, Pua, Doi Phu Kha & Bo Kluea | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 3-day, 2-night Nan itinerary in Thailand: old town and Wat Phumin on day one, Pua and the 1256 sky road to Bo Kluea on day two, Doi Phu Kha on day three. With times, distances and real stops.
keywords: Nan 3 day itinerary, things to do in Nan, Pua, Doi Phu Kha, Bo Kluea, route 1256 sky road
intro: Nan is an easy place to travel if you plan the route well, because the town, Pua, Doi Phu Kha and Bo Kluea all sit in different directions. Zig-zagging between them all day just wears you out. This plan runs as a loop: spend day one finishing the old town and the temples, head up to Pua on day two and take the 1256 sky road across to Bo Kluea and Sapan, sleep over on that side, then stop at Doi Phu Kha on day three before looping back. It works best if you drive yourself or rent a car in Nan town.

blocks.html: Before we start, honestly Nan is most fun with your own wheels, because the sights are spread far apart and public transport to places like Bo Kluea and Sapan barely exists. If you fly into Nan Nakhon airport, rent a car in town from day one. This plan is built as a loop so you never backtrack the same road, and it already leaves time for photo stops along the way.

items: Day 1 — Nan town Walk the old town, visit Wat Phumin and Wat Phra That Chae Haeng, climb Wat Phra That Khao Noi for the view, and stroll the walking street in the evening (if it falls on Fri–Sun)
Day 2 — Pua → Bo Kluea Drive up to Pua for coffee at a Tai Lue village, take the 1256 sky road past the viewpoints, drop down to Bo Kluea to see the salt boiling, and sleep in Sapan
Day 3 — Doi Phu Kha → back Enjoy the cool morning in Sapan, stop at the Doi Phu Kha 1715 viewpoint, then loop back to Nan town or the airport

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Nan old town — temples, strolling, walking street

items.activity: Start at Wat Phumin in the heart of the old town
items.note: The only cross-shaped (jaturamuk) ordination hall in Thailand, with four Buddha images facing the four directions. The spot everyone photographs is the mural known as the Whispering Couple (Pu Man Ya Man). Free to enter.

items.activity: Wander the old town and stop at Nan National Museum
items.note: Out front there is a frangipani arch that photographs well, and the museum holds the city's famous black elephant tusk. Entry is around 100 THB, and it's walking distance from Wat Phumin.

items.activity: Lunch — northern Thai food in town
items.note: Try khao soi, gaeng hang lay, or nam prik num with crispy pork rinds. There are plenty of local spots along Sumonthewarat Road and around the old town.

items.activity: Visit Wat Phra That Chae Haeng, about 3 km out of town
items.note: This is the temple linked to those born in the Year of the Rabbit. The golden chedi stands out and it's the city's most important stupa, popular with people coming to pray for blessings.

items.activity: Climb Wat Phra That Khao Noi for the town view
items.note: It sits on a hill on the west side of town, with a large standing Buddha and a viewpoint looking out over the whole of Nan. The light is lovely in the late afternoon and people come up for sunset.

items.activity: Walk the Kad Khuang Mueang Nan walking street in front of Wat Phumin
items.note: It only runs Fri–Sat–Sun. If your dates line up you can eat local food and sit khantoke-style. If not, just find a dinner spot in town instead.

blocks.title: Where to sleep on night one
blocks.html: The first night is easiest in Nan town, close to the temples, restaurants and the car rental spots. Options range from old-town homestays to hotels along the Nan River. Check what's available on our Nan hotels page.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Pua → Route 1256 sky road → Bo Kluea → Sapan

items.activity: Leave Nan town heading north to Pua, about 60 km, roughly an hour and a bit
items.note: Fill up the tank before you go, because petrol stations are scarce along the sky road.

items.activity: Stop in Pua for coffee at Lamduan Phathong — Tai Lue Village Coffee, Sila Laeng
items.note: This is one of Pua's well-known Tai Lue weaving shops, with a café out back set in the rice fields and framed by the mountains. You can browse the woven cloth and pick up souvenirs in the same place.

items.activity: Alternative: Rong Bom Pua Cafe and Eatery in Pua district
items.note: A café set in an old tobacco-curing barn that roasts its own Nan coffee, open 09:00–16:30. If you like old-building cafés, swap this in or just add it on.

items.activity: Get onto Route 1256, the Pua–Bo Kluea sky road
items.note: It's a winding climb with mountains stacked up on both sides. Drive slowly and watch the bends; there are several pull-offs for photos along the way.

items.activity: Lunch around Sapan / Bo Kluea at a rice-field-view spot
items.note: The Sapan area has restaurants and cafés overlooking the terraced fields. Keep the order simple, the view is the point, and prices vary by place so just ask.

items.activity: Visit Bo Kluea, the rock-salt wells, and the old craft of boiling salt up in the mountains
items.note: These ancient salt wells are hundreds of years old and salt is still boiled the traditional way. You can buy mountain rock salt and salt flakes as souvenirs here.

items.activity: Check into a Sapan homestay and wander the village
items.note: Sapan is a small village in a valley with terraced fields and a stream. Most stays are simple homestays focused on the view and the quiet. Book ahead in the cool season.

blocks.title: The truth about stays around Bo Kluea and Sapan
blocks.html: Most places here are homestays, the rooms aren't fancy, the phone signal drops in patches, and in the cool season (Nov–Jan) they fill up fast. If you're coming then, book a month or two ahead rather than turning up and hoping.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Doi Phu Kha, the 1715 viewpoint, then back

items.activity: Wake up to the cool morning in Sapan, and with luck mist drifting over the fields
items.note: In the cool season there's a chance of a thin sea of mist. Get your shots early before the sun gets strong.

items.activity: Pack up and head back along Route 1256 toward Pua and Doi Phu Kha
items.note: The view is different from a different angle on the way back, and the drive feels easier now that you know the road.

items.activity: Stop at the 1715 viewpoint in Doi Phu Kha National Park
items.note: The name comes from its height, 1,715 metres above sea level, looking out over rows of sharp distant peaks. There's a car park, restrooms and a souvenir shop. Entry is around 40 THB.

items.activity: Explore more of Doi Phu Kha National Park
items.note: If you come in Feb–Mar you might catch the Chomphu Phu Kha blossom, found only here. There are short forest trails and Chomphu Phu Kha trees along the road.

items.activity: Come down off the mountain back toward Nan town, grabbing lunch on the way
items.note: From Doi Phu Kha back to Nan town is about 1.5–2 hours depending on your stops.

items.activity: Buy souvenirs in Nan town before you leave
items.note: Popular Nan souvenirs are processed wampee fruit, Tai Lue woven cloth, and Nan coffee. Shop in town before heading to the airport or your bus home.

blocks.html: The cool season, November to February, has the best weather, clear skies and a real shot at the sea of mist at Doi Phu Kha and Sapan, but it's also busy and rooms fill up fast. The rainy season, roughly June to September, is when the terraced fields are at their greenest and Pua and Sapan look gorgeous, but the sky road gets slippery and the mist can close in thick in places, so drive carefully.

items: Car rental A small car runs around 1,000–1,500 THB/day, cheaper split among a group
2 nights' stay A homestay or mid-range hotel runs around 700–1,500 THB/night
Entry fees Doi Phu Kha around 40 THB, the museum around 100 THB, most temples free
Food A local meal runs around 60–150 THB, café coffee around 60–90 THB
Fuel Budget around 800–1,200 THB for this loop, depending on distance and your car

blocks.title: Driving the 1256 sky road
blocks.html: This road really is beautiful, but it has plenty of bends and steep grades. Use a low gear on the descents and don't ride the brakes. Set off early to share the road with fewer cars, and avoid driving at night because there's little lighting and the mist can roll in any time.

faq.q: Do I need my own car for a 3-day Nan trip?
faq.a: A car is strongly recommended, whether you drive your own or rent one in Nan town, because places like Pua, Doi Phu Kha, Bo Kluea and Sapan are far apart and hard to reach by public transport. If you don't drive, you may have to hire a car with a driver by the day.

faq.q: Where should I sleep over the 2 nights?
faq.a: This plan puts the first night in Nan town so you can finish the temples and old town, and the second night on the Sapan or Bo Kluea side, so you get the cool morning and don't have to backtrack far.

faq.q: Is Route 1256, the sky road, hard to drive?
faq.a: It's a fairly steep, winding mountain climb. A confident everyday driver will be fine, but you need to go slowly, use a low gear on the descents, and avoid driving at night or when the mist closes in thick.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Nan?
faq.a: The cool season, Nov–Feb, has the best weather and a shot at the sea of mist, but it's busy and rooms fill up fast. The rainy season makes the terraced fields beautifully green, but the roads get slippery and the mist comes in often.

faq.q: Is there an entry fee for Doi Phu Kha?
faq.a: Doi Phu Kha National Park charges around 40 THB per person for Thai visitors. The 1715 viewpoint sits on Route 1256 and has a car park, restrooms and a souvenir shop.
